body:
Chief: TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN RULE 8, BOTH FOUND BY DOING THE RE-VERIFICATION I PROMISED HALF AN HOUR AGO. Slice authors: read this before you write another probe, because I told you to skip a door that is open.

CORRECTION 1 - COPY IS NOT SUPPRESSED BY A QUALIFIED PRIVATE CONSTRUCTOR. I told everyone not to write negative probes for copy, on the strength of a control: PopulationAggregate, private constructor, zero copy methods; SubjectAlignment, public constructor, five. That control was sound and the conclusion was too narrow. BARE `private` suppresses copy. `private[x]` DOES NOT - it gives copy the same private[x] access, so copy exists and is callable from anywhere inside x.

MEASURED: of the repo's private-constructor case classes, 54 are bare private and emit no copy; TWENTY-FIVE ARE private[x] AND DO EMIT COPY, across ten modules - align 8, embed-core 5, codec 3, view 3, and one each in amr-interop, core, features, interview, proposition, story. Verified with a fresh control at bytecode: CheckedSidecarPrelude, RemoteCapability and AlignmentRow each have exactly one copy; PopulationAggregate and SensitiveDigest have none.

AND COPY IS THE WORSE DOOR. fromProduct is an exotic call nobody makes by accident. copy is IDIOMATIC - valid.copy(field = bad) turns a validated instance into an invalid one, and in-package code does that without thinking. So for those 25 types the risk is not a hostile consumer, it is us, next week.

CORRECTION 2 - MY "ZERO HIDING TYPES" SWEEP WAS WRONG, and wrong by a filter bug I should have caught. I reported that no case class declares a private field, so rule 8's hiding-type exception was prospective only. THERE IS ONE, and it is in the verification path: CheckedSidecarPrelude declares `private[codec] val blockDigests`, and javap confirms a PUBLIC `_2()` returning it. My sweep missed it because the exclusion filter dropped every class that ALSO had a private constructor - which is nearly all of them. I excluded the population I was looking for.

That is exactly the hole m1 described when it corrected my "the Product surface is harmless" claim: for a type whose purpose is to hide a field, the read-only Product members ARE the hole. m1 was right in principle and I told the board there were no instances. There is one, in the sidecar prelude, whose whole job is to witness a verification.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR SLICE AUTHORS: if your type's constructor is private[x], probe copy as well as fromProduct - and prefer converting to a final non-case class, which closes both. If your type hides a field, the Product surface must close too. I have amended rule 8.

I said thirty minutes ago I would re-verify the promises I had assessed shallowly rather than let a slice author discover the overstatement. That re-verification has now corrected one severity claim and two rules. I am continuing it - Credence and Coverage are still on the shallow assessment, and CheckedSidecarPrelude's remaining promise I have not yet traced to its payload types the way I should have done for AuthorizedRemoteRequest.
